newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: HOWARD PUSHING FOR RELIEF ON BRITISH PENSION BURDEN

Britain's new government has hinted that it may be prepared to move on a long-standing financial disagreement with Australia: Britain's refusal to top-up the pensions of its migrants to Australia. British Prime Minister, Tony Blair, has agreed to continue negotiations on the issue, after a meeting with his Australian counterpart, John Howard, who is in London. Mr Howard says officials from both countries will hold talks on the pension funding, which costs Australia $80 million a year.

The New South Wales Premier's plan to push ahead with the privatisation of the state's electricity assets before the ALP's conference in October, has been dealt a severe blow. The six Left ministers of the cabinet are supporting 26 left and right-wing backbenchers who have warned they will vote against the sale of Pacific Power in parliament, unless the party's annual conference has fully debated the issue.
The action by the MPs contradicts Bob Carr's assertion that the proposed sell-off of power assets will be endorsed by Cabinet and there will be no need for the plan to go to the conference

The Federal Department responsible for medical reports on Social Security claimants and government employees has been corporatised. The Australian Government Health Service is now officially a corporation created from the Health Department. It is called "Health Services Australia."

Breath test ignition locks will begin national trials in July, using 300 South Australian drivers. State Transport Minister Diana Laidlaw says the trial will start with volunteers, but the government may legislate to force convicted drink drivers to participate. Eventually all drink drivers could be forced to use the locks as part of their penalty. Ms Laidlaw says drivers who have lost their licences, but not yet reapplied will be invited to take part in the trial.

The mother of murdered Walgett nurse Sandra Hoare says she will prepare a victim impact statement for the judge who must sentence her daughter's killers. Cousins, Brendan and Vester Fernando, were yesterday found guilty by a jury of the murder of the 21-year-old nurse, who was raped and killed while working a night shift at the Walgett Hospital in 1994. The two cousins will be sentenced in the New South Wales Supreme Court on a date to be fixed.
GROG RUNNING NOT INCREASING NEAR ULURU
A member of an Aboriginal community near Uluru, or Ayers Rock, says grog-running has not increased since a ban on take-away liquor from a roadhouse 100 kilometres away.
The Curtin Springs roadhouse agreed to a six-month trial of the restrictions, but claims alcohol is still available from people bringing it into the dry area from Alice Springs.
Chair of the Mutitjulu community, Mantatjara Wison says some drinkers have been travelling 500 kilometres to Alice Springs. But she says, they do not bring grog back with them.
